A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRA research, with matching authors, central questions and benchmark experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and all appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-task accuracy, WikiText-103 perplexity and attention analyses in Section 3, Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds language-model attention analyses and measured runtime comparisons in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The specified attention logits change from S' + D' in v1 Equation 9 to S' + log(D') in v4 Equation 10. This is a non-equivalent scoring revision, although ReLU thresholding, contextual distance counting and the learned forget gate remain. Newly disclosed implementation details do not establish additional procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Flip-Flop with IID, dense and sparse conditions, Induct, Copy, Flip-Flops++ and WikiText-103. The new attention and runtime analyses introduce no identified dataset, domain or distinct task requirement.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator membership: NoPE, APE, REL, RoPE, Label, FoT, Diff and CoPE. The new runtime comparison reuses RoPE; newly discussed approaches such as FlashAttention are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.6 revises the reported language-model parameter count from approximately 100 million to 80 million, while retaining the stated layers, heads and embedding dimensions; this does not establish resizing or rerunning. Appendix D adds a timing protocol using tiny and medium configurations, 20,000 steps, window size 256 and batch size 64.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figure 3 add qualitative analyses of dense, mixed and sparse language-model attention heads. Appendix D adds runtime-overhead measurements at two model sizes. These supplement the retained synthetic attention analysis without introducing a broad ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: The retained benchmark results preserve their four-initialisation reporting, numerical uncertainty summaries and four-seed perplexity plot. No new statistical procedure is introduced; Appendix D's timings have no stated repeat count or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original figure results are unchanged. Appendix D newly reports RoPE/TRA runtimes of 58.73/65.88 minutes for tiny models and 156.34/178.19 minutes for medium models over 20,000 steps. Appendix C adds qualitative findings relating attention sparsity to weaker temporal decay.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 revises the mathematical definition of attention logits by applying log to the positional weight, rather than adding that weight directly. The new explicit cumulative-sum equation restates the operation already described in v1; neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: combining selective sparsity with contextual relative distance to improve length generalisation. Claims of solving the Flip-Flop benchmark and generalising language modelling to 32 times the training context are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix C interprets dense heads as favouring local positional attention and sparse heads as favouring content, with token-dependent decay. Appendix D newly acknowledges runtime overhead relative to RoPE and explicitly qualifies proposed tiling and FlashAttention-style optimisations as speculative.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the previously missing appendix implementation: a PyTorch listing documenting Q/K normalisation, per-head gates, dropout placement and handling of fully masked rows. Appendix D adds hardware and timing-configuration details. The repository pointer is replaced by an appendix-code reference, while the existing hyperparameters move from Appendix A to B.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds positioning against fixed-pattern sparse attention, sparse probability mappings and ReLU attention, citing Child, Zaheer, Nawrot, Peters and Zhang. Appendix D adds FlashAttention references, and the ALiBi comparison becomes more explicit. The central novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 expands the contextual-distance explanation and forget-gate motivation, rewrites the FoT description and makes local language corrections. New appendices extend the document, but the main section order and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the boxed implementation listing and Figure 3 with three groups of attention heatmaps. Existing tables and figure images are retained, with some relocation relative to surrounding text, clearer matrix brackets and publication headers. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The supplied implementation and clearer method explanation improve technical inspectability, while the new attention analysis and measured runtime costs strengthen transparency about behaviour and practical limitations. These are useful, bounded improvements to otherwise retained benchmark evidence. Replacing the repository pointer with a core code excerpt is an access tradeoff, and the PDFs leave unresolved whether the equation and parameter-count revisions reflect corrections or changed experiments.
